name: 蔡坦欣
objective:
本課程旨在進一步提升學生於學術會議與研討場合中以英語進行口頭報告、簡報發表及互動應對之能力。課程聚焦學術會議常見之發表形式，包括論文口頭發表、海報發表、研究摘要說明、短講及問答交流，並著重學術口語論述之組織、研究重點之清楚傳達、論點整合、聽眾互動與現場應答技巧。透過會議情境模擬、口頭報告、海報發表演練與回應活動，學生將強化其學術英語口語表達、簡報呈現與會議溝通能力，並建立參與國際學術交流之實務基礎。
This course aims to further develop students’ ability to deliver oral reports, conference presentations, and academic briefings in English in conference and seminar settings. It focuses on common forms of academic conference communication, including paper presentations, poster sessions, research summaries, short talks, and question-and-answer exchanges. Special emphasis is placed on organizing academic oral discourse, presenting research clearly, integrating key arguments, engaging with audiences, and responding effectively in live academic settings. Through conference simulations, oral presentation practice, poster presentation tasks, and response activities, students will strengthen their spoken academic English, presentation delivery, and conference communication skills, building a practical foundation for participation in international academic events.
schedule:
Week 1: Course orientation; introduction to academic oral communication; diagnostic speaking activity.
Week 2: Unit 1 Breaking the Ice — Small Talk on Campus: opening and continuing conversations.
Week 3: Unit 1 — Introducing oneself and others; changing topics naturally in campus conversations.
Week 4: Unit 1 — Small Talk at a Conference: starting conversations with professionals and discussing academic fields.
Week 5: Unit 1 — Ending conversations politely and exchanging contact information; role-play practice.
Week 6: Unit 2 Asking for Guidance — Discussing course planning with a professor; asking for academic advice.
Week 7: Unit 2 — Explaining personal plans, ideas, and considerations in professor-student conversations.
Week 8: Unit 2 — Online discussion with a professor about learning issues; video meeting language and etiquette.
Week 9: Midterm oral assessment: professor consultation or conference small-talk role play.
Week 10: Midterm feedback and language review; improving fluency, clarity, and interaction strategies.
Week 11: Unit 3 Exchanging Ideas and Negotiating Tasks — In-class group discussion; setting discussion goals.
Week 12: Unit 3 — Expressing agreement and disagreement; asking questions and using critical thinking.
Week 13: Unit 3 — Teamwork discussion; negotiating task division and giving concrete suggestions.
Week 14: Unit 3 — Expressing concerns, confirming agreement, and reaching group consensus.
Week 15: Unit 4 Expanding Your Opportunities — Self-introduction; explaining motivation and relevant experience.
Week 16: Unit 4 — Highlighting personal strengths and describing future goals.
Week 17: Unit 4 — Interview questions and answers; connecting interests, goals, and experience.
Week 18: Final oral assessment: self-introduction and interview task; course reflection.
scorePolicy:
The final grade for this course consists of two major parts: instructor-based assessment, which accounts for 80% of the final grade, and the university English proficiency exam, which accounts for 20% of the final grade.

Instructor-based assessment: 80%

Attendance and participation: 16%. Students are expected to attend class regularly and participate actively in pair work, group discussion, textbook activities, BESTEP-style tasks, and speaking practice.

Vocabulary, reading, and in-class exercises: 20%. Students will complete textbook-based vocabulary exercises, reading comprehension tasks, collocation practice, and activities involving textual and visual information such as tables, charts, graphs, diagrams, or short academic texts.

Homework and preparation: 16%. Assignments may include vocabulary review, short reading responses, data description practice, writing tasks, short recordings, and preparation for discussions or presentations.

Midterm assessment: 12%. The midterm assessment will be based on the first half of the semester and may include vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short oral or written task.

Final assessment: 16%. The final assessment may include a short presentation, written response, reading task, vocabulary review, or integrated textual and visual information task. Students will be evaluated on clarity, organization, accuracy, content understanding, and appropriate use of course-related English.

University English proficiency exam: 20%

The university English proficiency exam accounts for 20% of the final grade. Students are required to follow the university’s official regulations and schedule for this exam.
materials:
Required textbook:
LTTC. 學術英語 Power Up：必學口語溝通與簡報技能 / EAP Power Up: Essential Oral Interaction and Presentation Skills. The Language Training & Testing Center.

This semester will cover Units 1–4 only. Units 5–8 will be reserved for the second semester of this year-long course.

Supplementary materials may include instructor-designed worksheets, vocabulary lists, speaking task sheets, role-play prompts, assessment rubrics, and presentation slides.
延伸教學與資源: ● 混成學習 (Blended Learning) 課程結合實體授課與線上學習（同步視訊／非同步活動）。Combines face-to-face instruction with online learning (including synchronous video sessions or asynchronous activities).● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching) 強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.● 數位教材資源應用 (Application of Digital Resources) 採用影音多媒體或具開放授權之資源（如 OCW、開放教科書）作為主要或輔助教材。Adopts multimedia or open-licensed resources (e.g., OCW, Open Textbooks) as primary or supplementary teaching materials.● 數位科技融入 (Digital Technology Integration) 運用生成式 AI、VR/AR、IoT、IRS 等新興科技輔助教學與評量。Utilizes emerging technologies such as Generative AI, VR/AR, IoT, and IRS (Interactive Response Systems) to facilitate teaching and assessment.
